newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ATHLETICS-ROMANIAN FEDERATION BACKS TWO-YEAR NEGURA BAN.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-ROMANIAN FEDERATION BACKS TWO-YEAR NEGURA BAN.

text.p: Romanian athletics officials are defending their decision to impose a two-year drug ban on women's cross-country champion Iulia Negura, rather than the four-year suspension of the sport's ruling body.

Romanian Athletics Federation (FRA) officials said on Friday Negura had been punished for a first offence with local rules, which prevail over the International Amateur Athletic Federation (IAAF) sanctions.

Negura, 30, was banned until December 1998 by the FRA and stripped of her gold medal after testing positive for the anabolic steriod stanozolol at the 1996 European cross-country championships in Charleroi, Belgium.
The Romanian national team also lost their silver medal, but IAAF spokesman Giorgio Reinieri insisted the punishment meted out to Negura should have been harsher.

"The reality is we(IAAF) have a rule which is unenforceable in many countries. We have more and more places where it's impossible for our rules to be applied. State law prevails," he told Reuters from Monte Carlo.
"This is a problem that does not only concern Romania, but so many other countries," he said.
FRA president Iolanda Balas said in Bucharest the FRA had sent the IAAF a copy of Romanian sports rules adopted last year, which allow for shorter bans for first doping cases.
Under those rules, a first doping offence is punished with a two-year ban, with a life ban following in case of a repeat.
Balas said such rules were not unique in the world.
"Spain, for instance also has two-year bans for doping at a first offence, and the United States has milder punishments."
Both Negura, who was punished for her first offence in a long career, and her coach Dorin Melinte have denied she had taken a banned substance.
